recent_posts.title: Manage your K8s cluster with your phone | Omni via Nautik
Scaling Kubernetes requires predictability, not operational heroics
recent_posts.summary: A webinar-style conversation between Cedaro Labs' CPO and a solutions architect exploring why Kubernetes operations become unsustainable at scale when relying on manual heroics and undocumented changes. The discussion covers how configuration drift, burnout, and snowflake clusters emerge over time, and how Talos Linux — a minimalistic, immutable OS with only 50 binaries designed exclusively to run Kubernetes — addresses these problems. By replacing general-purpose Linux with an API-only, declarative, state-driven OS, teams eliminate SSH access, reduce CVE surface area, and gain deterministic cluster upgrades. A live demo shows how a full node config fits in 66 lines and how drift can be detected and reversed instantly.

recent_posts.title: Remotely configure Talos Linux with HTTP
recent_posts.summary: Talos Linux supports a lesser-known feature where the machine configuration can be fetched from a remote HTTP endpoint at boot time, rather than being embedded directly in kernel parameters. When Talos starts and network becomes available, it reaches out to a configured URL, sending device identifiers like MAC address, UUID, hostname, and serial number. A remote server can use these variables to match devices and return the appropriate full or partial config. The walkthrough demonstrates building a custom Talos image with the endpoint baked in via the image factory, running a simple demo web server that maps device variables to YAML config files, and using Omni's partial join config to automatically onboard a bare-metal machine into a cluster. The feature also supports OAuth authentication, displaying a QR code at the console for device authorization. This approach is particularly useful for pre-flashing devices and shipping them globally without knowing their final destination or customer assignment in advance.

recent_posts.title: Talos Omni Kubernetes stack, completely air-gapped
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive walkthrough of setting up a fully air-gapped Talos Omni Kubernetes stack, covering every component from scratch: generating a custom root CA and TLS certificates, deploying a private container registry, running an on-premises image factory, configuring OIDC authentication with Dex, and finally bootstrapping a Kubernetes cluster. The guide emphasizes preserving container image digests when mirroring (using crane), handling SELinux permissions, managing firewall rules, and seeding the internal registry from an internet-connected admin machine without ever directly bridging the air gap. A physical machine is booted from a custom ISO embedding the CA and Omni join token to demonstrate end-to-end cluster creation.

recent_posts.title: Multi-doc configurations with Talos Linux
recent_posts.summary: Multi-doc configuration in Talos Linux allows breaking up the traditional single YAML machine config file into smaller, modular configuration documents. This approach enables configuring specific aspects (certificates, network, filesystem) before Kubernetes installation and avoids kernel argument limitations. Starting with Talos 1.12, network configuration extensively uses multi-doc format. The feature maintains backward compatibility while enabling use cases like joining Omni instances through SideroLink configuration. Multi-doc configs can be sent individually to the API or concatenated with the main machine config during installation, with patches managed as separate files for better configuration management.

recent_posts.title: Temporary remote logging for debugging
recent_posts.summary: A practical technique for extracting logs from Talos systems during maintenance or installation phases when SSH and API servers are unavailable. The method involves configuring remote logging to stream kernel and service logs to a TCP endpoint, which can be captured using netcat and saved for debugging or support purposes. This approach is particularly useful during system provisioning before full machine configuration is applied.

recent_posts.title: Roche: Cutting the Cord: An Air-Gapped Journey with Talos and Cilium
recent_posts.summary: Roche's platform engineering team shares their journey implementing air-gapped Kubernetes deployments for healthcare environments with strict data privacy requirements. They evolved from pure GitOps to OCI artifact-based delivery, deployed Zot registry as a Talos system extension with containerd mirroring, and leveraged Cilium network policies with traffic redirection to transparently route cluster traffic to local registries. The solution maintains a unified architecture for both connected and disconnected clusters, enabling secure upgrades and application delivery through signed bundles delivered by field engineers.

recent_posts.title: Applying modern DevOps and Platform Engineering practices to a homelab with Talos Linux and Omni
recent_posts.summary: A senior engineering manager shares his journey building a homelab using Talos Linux and Omni, demonstrating how modern platform engineering principles can simplify Kubernetes deployment. The talk emphasizes simplicity over complexity, showing how Talos Linux (an immutable, API-driven OS with no SSH) and Omni (a management platform) abstract away infrastructure complexity. Through a live demo, he provisions a hybrid cloud cluster spanning both cloud VMs and local Proxmox machines with just a few clicks, illustrating how proper abstractions enable teams to focus on application development rather than infrastructure management.

recent_posts.title: Promptly: From Zero to Scalable: Accelerated On-Premise Infrastructure with Omni and GitOps
recent_posts.summary: DevOps engineers from Promptly Health demonstrate deploying 50 Kubernetes clusters in under 7 minutes using Talos Linux and Omni. They built a federated health data network requiring on-premise, infrastructure-agnostic deployment across hundreds of clusters. The solution combines Talos as the Kubernetes distribution with Omni for cluster lifecycle management and ArgoCD for GitOps-based application deployment. Key challenges included configuring ArgoCD's hub-spoke model to work with Omni's unified API endpoint by adding query parameters to server URLs. They automated the entire workflow using Omni and ArgoCD client SDKs, from cluster creation through application deployment, with plans to integrate Cilium CNI and Harbor registry.

recent_posts.title: Disk to Data to DR
recent_posts.summary: A technical walkthrough demonstrating how to configure persistent storage in Kubernetes using Talos OS with raw volume partitioning and Rook Ceph. The presentation covers the Container Storage Interface (CSI), creating custom disk partitions to optimize storage allocation, deploying stateful workloads like MongoDB, and implementing backup and disaster recovery strategies using Kasten. Includes a live demo showing data protection and restoration of a Pac-Man application with MongoDB backend.
